subject: Reasoning
question:
Read the statements carefully and assume it to be true. Then examine the two conclusions given below it and decide which conclusion(s), if any, logically follow from the statement.

Statements:

1. The Internet has become an integral part of our lives.

2. Yet there is ongoing debate over whether the Internet is a boon or a curse.

Conclusions:

I. It is difficult to imagine life without the Internet.

II. The constant debate on the Internet is unnecessary.
question_hi:
कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इन्हें सत्य मानिए। फिर नीचे दिए गए दो निष्कर्षों की जाँच कीजिए और तय कीजिए कि कौन-सा/से निष्कर्ष, यदि कोई हो, कथन का तार्किक रूप से अनुसरण करता/करते है/हैं।

कथन:

1. इंटरनेट हमारे जीवन का अभिन्न अंग बन गया है।

2. फिर भी इस पर बहस जारी है कि इंटरनेट वरदान है या अभिशाप।

निष्कर्ष:

I. इंटरनेट के बिना जीवन की कल्पना करना कठिन है।

II. इंटरनेट पर निरंतर बहस अनावश्यक है।
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both Conclusions I and II follow
options_hi: केवल निष्कर्ष I अनुसरण करता है
न तो निष्कर्ष I और न ही II अनुसरण करता है
निष्कर्ष I और II दोनों अनुसरण करते हैं
केवल निष्कर्ष II अनुसरण करता है
explanation: Correct answer: Option A — Only Conclusion I follows
explanation_hi: Correct answer: Option A — Only Conclusion I follows

subject: Reasoning
question:
Examine the eligibility guidelines set for the government tablet distribution scheme by assessing the applications of Student X and Student Y against the stated criteria. Identify which student meets the selection requirements considering the budget constraint given.

Eligibility: A government scheme: "Free tablet computers are provided to students who score 90%+ in Class 10 AND belong to a family with an income < ₹2L/year."

Student X: Scored 92%, family income ₹1.9L/year.

Student Y: Scored 89%, family income ₹1.5L/year.

Budget Constraint: The remaining tablets are only enough for 1 student.
question_hi:
सरकारी टैबलेट वितरण योजना के लिए निर्धारित पात्रता दिशानिर्देशों की जाँच कीजिए और बताए गए मानदंडों के आधार पर छात्र X और छात्र Y के आवेदनों का आकलन कीजिए। बजट बाधा को ध्यान में रखते हुए पहचानिए कि कौन-सा छात्र चयन आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करता है।

पात्रता: एक सरकारी योजना: "कक्षा 10 में 90%+ अंक प्राप्त करने वाले तथा ₹2L/वर्ष से कम आय वाले परिवार के छात्रों को निःशुल्क टैबलेट कंप्यूटर प्रदान किए जाते हैं।"

छात्र X: 92% अंक, पारिवारिक आय ₹1.9L/वर्ष।

छात्र Y: 89% अंक, पारिवारिक आय ₹1.5L/वर्ष।

बजट बाधा: शेष टैबलेट केवल एक छात्र के लिए पर्याप्त हैं।
options: Give to Student X because they met the academic criteria.
Give to Student Y because they are financially weaker.
Give to neither, as both do not satisfy all criteria.
Split the cost and provide a cheaper device to both.
options_hi: छात्र X को दें क्योंकि वह शैक्षणिक मानदंड पूरा करता है।
छात्र Y को दें क्योंकि वह आर्थिक रूप से कमज़ोर है।
किसी को भी न दें, क्योंकि दोनों सभी मानदंड पूरे नहीं करते।
लागत को विभाजित करें और दोनों को एक सस्ता उपकरण प्रदान करें।
explanation: Correct answer: Option A — Give to Student X because they met the academic criteria.
explanation_hi: Correct answer: Option A — Give to Student X because they met the academic criteria.

कथन:

सभी पेन लैपटॉप हैं।

The menstrual cycle, frequently distilled into reductive explanations within mainstream discourse, constitutes a complex, finely-tuned hormonal symphony that underpins female reproductive viability. Typically spanning around 28 days—though significant interindividual variability persists—the cycle is anatomically and biochemically demarcated into four sequential phases: menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, and the luteal phase.

Menstruation initiates with the systematic desquamation of the functional layer of the endometrium, an event precipitated by the precipitous decline in circulating levels of estrogen and progesterone following an unfertilized ovulatory event. Thereafter, during the follicular phase, anterior pituitary secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) catalyses the recruitment and maturation of ovarian follicles. A single dominant follicle subsequently prevails, secreting escalating quantities of estrogen to promote proliferative thickening of the endometrial lining in anticipation of potential zygote implantation.

Mid-cycle, ovulation ensues, triggered by an acute surge of luteinizing hormone (LH), culminating in the release of an oocyte into the fallopian tube — a transient but critical window of maximal fertility. In the absence of fertilization, the luteal phase commences: the residual follicular structure, now termed the corpus luteum, secretes progesterone to stabilize the endometrial architecture. Without embryonic implantation, corpus luteum regression ensues, hormonal concentrations diminish sharply, and the cyclical endometrial shedding recommences.

Despite the endogenous predictability of this sequence, the menstrual cycle exhibits considerable vulnerability to extrinsic perturbations — including psychosocial stressors, systemic illnesses, and environmental variables — underscoring the intricate interplay between endocrine function and broader homeostatic mechanisms.
